title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing - Q4 2026
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements), high-level design specifications, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging notes, and the latest release notes for the Unified Inference product (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private). It is designed as a single source of truth for product managers, engineering leads, GTM, and key stakeholders.

Goals

- Deliver a unified inference surface that provides consistent latency, cost controls, and deployment flexibility across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private.
- Reduce per-token unit costs by 20% vs. baseline (Q1 2026 baseline) through batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations.
- Provide first-class rollout tooling (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) and observable regressions tied to eval prompt sets.

Audience

- Product Managers, Engineering, Developer Experience, Sales/GTM, and Customer Success.

1) Product Requirements (PRD)

Summary:
The Unified Inference product aims to expose a single API surface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with consistent SLAs and cost controls across deployment modes.

Primary use cases:
- Low-latency chat for consumer-facing applications (p99 < 400ms for short responses on Hosted tier)
- High-throughput batch embedding pipelines for search indexing
- Regulated on-prem inference for enterprise customers with strict data residency

Core requirements (must-have):
1. Single REST/SDK API with feature parity for text, chat, embeddings, streaming, and tool-calls.
2. Model catalog with metadata, performance profile (latency/cost per token), and compatible quantization variants.
3. SLOs and quotas per plan: Hosted (p99 latency <= 600ms small requests, 99.9% uptime); Dedicated (throughput SLA + 99.95% uptime); Private (availability target defined per contract).
4. Routing and fallback policies: region-aware, cost-aware, and capacity fallback to compatible model variants.
5. Observability: per-route token/cost breakdowns, traces, and alerting hooks.
6. Rollout controls: canary, A/B splits, automatic rollback on quality regressions or SLO violations.
7. Pricing controls: per-token pricing, reserved capacity commitments, and enterprise packaging for Private.
8. Security/compliance: KMS/HSM integration, audit logging, RBAC for administrative ops, and SOC2 evidence for hosted product.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
- Scalability to 10M QPS token-rate across fleet during peak.
- 20% tail-latency improvement via kernel selection and batching strategies compared to baseline.
- Production safety: automated rate-limiting and cost-surge protections to prevent billing shocks.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end test coverage for API compatibility across modes.
- Benchmarks: generation throughput and latency reports for top 10 catalog models.
- Pricing page and calculator available in Console for customers to estimate costs.

2) High-level Design Specs

Architecture overview:
- API Gateway (hosted control plane) -> Routing layer -> Serving runtime (GPU-optimized pools) -> Cache layer (KV / prefix caching) -> Observability & Billing.

Key components and interfaces:
- Model Catalog Service: stores model metadata, performance profiles, quantization variants. API example: GET /models/{model_id}/profile -> returns latency/cost matrix per seq-len.
- Routing & Policy Engine: decides target model variant and route (hosted/dedicated/private) based on policy (latency, cost, region).
- Serving Runtime: supports continuous batching, KV cache management, kernel selection heuristics. Exposes gRPC control plane for deployments.

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Strong consistency vs. availability for routing decisions: prefer eventual consistency for catalog updates to avoid global disruptions during model onboarding.
- Batching aggressiveness: adaptive based on request type (interactive vs. batch) to balance latency and cost.

Spec snippets and examples:
- Example SDK call (Python):

```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.chat.create(model='rw-unified-small-v2', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Summarize the following...'}], stream=False)
```

- Example routing policy (YAML):

```yaml
policy_id: low_latency_us_east
priority: [regional_capacity, latency, cost]
fallbacks:
  - model_variant: rw-unified-medium-quant
    condition: capacity_exhausted
  - model_variant: rw-unified-small
    condition: latency_budget_exceeded
```

Observability surfaces required:
- Per-route latency and token cost (console dashboard)
- Trace correlation id -> kernel selection and batching decisions
- Quality regression alerts (linked to prompt set that triggered the regression)

3) Roadmap & Themes (Q1 2027 - Q3 2027)

Themes:
- Performance & Cost: intelligent batching, KV cache improvements, kernel autotuner.
- Enterprise readiness: Private automated install, expanded KMS/HSM integrations, compliance playbooks.
- Developer Experience: expanded SDKs, prompt evaluators, and release of Console pricing calculator.

Quarterly milestones (high level):
- Q1 2027: Release batch scheduler v2 (30% throughput improvement for large seq), Console pricing calculator beta, model-catalog performance profiles.
- Q2 2027: Private automated install (airgap support), reserved capacity contracts UI, rollout of kernel autotuner to Dedicated fleets.
- Q3 2027: Quality monitoring (prompt-set tied evals + regression alarms), rollout of cost-aware routing by default for Hosted.

Stakeholder checkpoints:
- Monthly product/eng syncs (Owners present: Aisha, Carlos, Lena).
- Roadmap review with GTM and Customer Success quarterly.

Dependencies and risks:
- Dependency: Kernel vendor updates (3rd party) for quantized ops; risk: delayed vendor SDK -> mitigations: fallbacks to alternate kernels.
- Dependency: Legal/compliance for on-prem support in EMEA; risk: contract review delays -> mitigation: template legal addendum.

4) Pricing & Packaging Notes

Pricing objectives:
- Simple to understand for developers (self-serve) with clear unit economics.
- Reserve capacity model for predictable enterprise spend.
- Add-ons for premium observability and extended retention.

Proposed pricing tiers (summary table):

| Tier | Billing model | Target customer | Key SLA | Typical price (USD) |
|------|---------------|-----------------|---------|---------------------|
| Free / Trial | free credits, usage cap | New devs | best-effort | $0 up to credits |
| Hosted Pay-as-you-go | per-token + per-request (streaming) | PLG users | p99 latency <= 600ms | $0.0006 / token (gen) |
| Dedicated Reserved | monthly commit + overage | Mid-market / Scale | throughput SLA + 99.95% uptime | custom (example: $20k/mo for 250k qps) |
| Private Enterprise | license + support + infra | Regulated enterprises | contractual SLA | enterprise pricing (negotiated) |

Add-ons:
- Extended observability (90-day retention): +$X/mo
- Compliance package (SOC2+ISO): one-time onboarding fee + recurring audit support fee

Pricing calculator example (console):
- Inputs: expected tokens/day, average seq len, expected concurrency, desired SLO tier.
- Output: estimated monthly spend + recommended deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated) and recommended quantization profile.

Sales guidance (packaging notes):
- For customers estimating > $10k/mo, recommend Dedicated or reserved discount guidance.
- Include migration playbook from Hosted -> Dedicated with configuration checklist (networking, capacity sizing, data residency).

Rollout & Rollback Procedures

1. Create release candidate and tag in repo (owners: eng-servicing + release manager).
2. Canary rollout to 1% of traffic in us-east for 24h; monitor SLOs and quality metrics.
3. Expand to 10% then 50% on successful health checks.
4. Full rollout with monitoring and CD pipeline gating.
5. Automatic rollback trigger: 5% increase in p99 latency or a detected quality regression above threshold (see quality gating thresholds below).

Quality gating thresholds:
- Latency: p99 increase > 10% over baseline for 2 consecutive measurement windows (15m).
- Quality: For critical prompt sets, regression AUC drop > 3% or per-prompt BLEU/ROUGE drop beyond threshold.
